thread:
alex: paging oncall, seeing p95/p99 jump for streaming responses to inference-hosted in us-west-2, started ~5m ago. clients reporting stalls and aborted streams.

maya: saw the same on dashboards, SLO alert fired. p95 ~1.2s -> 3.8s, p99 ~3.4s -> 9.6s. streaming tail latency spikes, but total tokens per sec steady.

oncall-bot: @here Incident created: INC-2025-187. Severity: seattle. Impact: streaming stalls and increased tail latency affecting ~2% of requests.

alex: initial grep of logs shows a spike in configfetch latency from control-plane: 503s for some feature flag reads, also many 429s from auth tokenstore.

infra-jen: that's interesting — controlplane metrics show a deck of retries to DB configstore at the same timeframe. Could be cascading backoff.

maya: posting quick traces:
```
trace_id: 0xabc123
infer_gw -> controlplane/config-fetch (latency 1200ms) -> tokenstore (429) -> db-pool-wait
```

alex: putting a temporary rule: route streaming requests to dedicated fallback model-variant (no featureflag checks) for affected customers. Will flip in console.

sre-lead: agreed. also disable non-essential config fetch by setting ENV OVERRIDE for control-plane to cache-local for 10m. Refer runbook step 3.

maya: applying canary config now. patch: `redwoodctl config set controlplane.flag_fetch_mode=local_cache --scope=canary`

incident-bot: Runbook applied: controlplane cache-local canary. Monitoring for 2m.

alex: immediate improvement on one shard: p95 dropped to 1.1s, p99 to 3.0s. Not fully resolved; looks like tokenstore 429s still present for some tenants.

maya: checking tokenstore — rate limits are spiking on the auth side. Maybe our retry storm earlier saturated connection pools. Tokenstore has per-tenant qps limits.

infra-jen: I can temporarily raise tokenstore per-tenant QPS for the most affected tenants if we want to buy time. Will need approval for emergency quota bump.

sre-lead: do it for the top 5 impacted orgs. list? maya, alex can you provide org ids with highest error rates?

maya: top offenders: org-1342, org-8401, org-9922, org-6230, org-4003. org-1342 accounts for ~45% of 429s.

alex: granting emergency bump for those five. infra-jen: please also enable tokenstore debug logging for 10m to capture request patterns.

infra-jen: quota bump applied + debug logging on.

maya: seeing gradual recovery: p95 now 0.9s, p99 2.1s, but streaming stall count still non-zero for a subset.

sre-lead: next: we should hard-fail feature-flag checks at the gateway for streaming path instead of deferring to control-plane; that will avoid added round trips. Can we patch a lightweight toggle?

alex: yeah I'll roll a gateway shortcut to skip FF fetch for streams with header `X-RW-FF-SKIP=true`. Will roll canary.

maya: rolling gateway canary now.

incident-bot: Gateway shortcut canary deployed to 10% of traffic.

maya: early numbers look promising — those streams see near baseline latencies.

alex: customer impact note: we saw aborted streams causing degraded UX for ~2% of requests; premium customers affected intermittently. No data leakage.

sre-lead: good. we'll continue monitoring. handoff plan: if metrics stay green for 20m, close this incident with postmortem. If we see another spike, escalate to oncall-ops.

maya: tagging for handoff to night oncall in 25m: @oncall-night. I'll prepare the short summary and mitigation timeline.

infra-jen: leaving tokenstore debug logs for triage. Will revert quota bump after 40m.

alex: summary for postmortem (will paste into INC): root cause likely retry/queueing cascade in controlplane -> tokenstore rate limits -> increased controlplane latency -> blocking streaming path. Mitigation: route affected traffic to FF-free model variant, canary local-cache flag, emergency tokenstore bump, gateway FF-skip canary.

sre-lead: thanks team. call out follow-ups: 1) add circuit-breaker on controlplane feature flag calls from streaming path; 2) improve tokenstore QPS autoscaling and backoff jitter; 3) baking FF caching in runtime for streaming.

maya: adding tasks to INC-2025-187. will include quant metrics for p95/p99 and affected orgs.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled to night oncall at 1755554360.

alex: I'm available for questions during handoff.

maya: final note: customer outreach queued for impacted premium orgs, CS on standby.

sre-lead: closing comments: incident moving to monitoring. keep thread open for 1h for any late regressions.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2025-187 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
